column6: Poolside with drinks; the holiday is the reason and the product is the preparation for being seen.
Bottles the size of a yacht; the absurdity is the scroll-stop and the brand is the only message.
Answering a comment about flyaways; the specificity of the complaint is what makes the answer credible.
Pre and after one use side by side; why didn't I buy this sooner is the regret being pre-installed.
Four functions in one bottle plus a Sephora line; she is clearing shelf space and checking availability.
A scalp brush shot like a serum; the tool is being admitted into a routine that used to be just bottles.
One object, one light, no copy; the price is being justified by how little the ad is willing to say.
A tumbler, a coaster and playing cards; the props describe an evening she wants to be hosting.
A coloured flute against pale sky; the glass is styled as sculpture rather than tableware.
Dining and entertaining named directly; the occasion is a dinner she is hosting, not a shelf she is filling.
A named artist collaboration in a rendered desert; the signature is what makes it collectible.
A candy jar with legs; the strangeness is the point and the collaboration is the permission.
The object emerging from a ribboned box; this is being bought for the moment it gets opened.
A single leaf and the wordmark; the brand is behaving like a fashion house rather than a homeware brand.
Flat cards next to a bag; the form factor is the pitch because it disappears into what she already carries.
Sold out then back then discounted; the sequence assumes she was watching and missed it.
Three hundred sprays a bottle; refillable is being priced in units rather than argued as a virtue.
Held like a pen; the object has to look good in a hand because that is where it will be seen.
Six botanicals listed by name; she reads a sanitiser the way she reads a serum.
Your skin deserves better sanitizer blames the category rather than her hands; the whole aisle is the villain.
